exercise1.prompt: Two tables of the same shape, one after the other.

hiddenCases.name: the index is renumbered rather than repeated

exercise1.hint: pd.concat takes the list. ignore_index=True is what stops two rows both being numbered 0.

questions.explain: Without it each piece keeps its own numbering, so a stacked table can have several rows labelled 0 -- which then breaks anything that looks a row up by label.

questions.prompt: One table has a column the other lacks. What does concat do?
choices: Includes the column, with gaps for the rows that lacked it
questions.explain: The result is the union of the columns. Checking for unexpected gaps afterwards is how you notice a source changed its schema.

questions.prompt: When is concat the right tool rather than merge?
choices: When the tables are the same shape and you want them end to end
questions.explain: concat stacks; merge matches on a key. Reaching for the wrong one usually shows up as a row count that makes no sense.
